decision: routed the Nitro question through figure-it-out with Prototype steps inside

decision: sent one agent to read Nitro's source at a pinned SHA before building anything
why: whether the shadow node survives depends on what nitrogen generates for views, which reading settles faster than a build

decision: done means a cited report on effort, pros, cons and keep-or-replace for the shadow node, a POC APK verified on the Pixel 10 Pro Fold with screenshots and video, and a benchmark of 5+ alternating runs per side

decision: used agent-device 0.21.31 via npx with its own state dir, and release APKs instead of Metro
why: the global agent-device is 0.21.8 and another session's Metro holds the main checkout; release builds also match how the PR #54 numbers were taken

decision: concluded from Nitro 0.37.1 source that Hybrid Views cannot host the panes or keep our shadow node
why: nitrogen generates a ConcreteViewShadowNode alias with a final descriptor, uses the State slot for props on Android, and mounts no children (issue #873 open)

decision: build two prototypes in one POC APK: a Kotlin Nitro HybridObject for the hinge stream beside the untouched shadow node, and a minimal Nitro Hybrid View given React children
why: the first is the only integration with a possible win, the second turns the children blocker into an observed result instead of a cited one

decision: skipped prototyping the Unistyles pattern (C++ HybridObject committing via UIManager::updateShadowTree)
why: it commits on the JS thread, the path PR #54 measured at 26 ms idle and 146 ms under JS load against 8.9 and 11.4 ms for the shadow node

decision: delegated the POC build to one agent with a fixed contract: shadow node byte-identical, hinge HybridObject reusing HingeTracker, one APK whose bench switches transport at runtime
why: the same binary for both transports means only the transport differs between runs

decision: built main with the PR #54 latency probe in a separate detached worktree for a main-vs-POC arrangement comparison
why: adding Nitro should leave the posture-to-drawn-frame path unchanged, and the PR #54 harness measures exactly that

decision: accepted the POC agent's build after checking its diff: cpp/, the JNI shadow node and react-native.config.js unchanged
why: the integrate claim needs the shadow node byte-identical

decision: Nitro Hybrid View with a React child crashed the release app on mount
why: SimpleViewManager cannot hold children, so panes cannot live in a Nitro view

decision: moved the bench status text out of the timed window
why: its 500 ms re-render only happened when samples arrived, which inflated main-thread CPU for fabric and nitro but not none
evidence: smoke runs: main 216 and 175 ms vs none 81, falling to about 80 under load

decision: added a sample-to-frame probe (HingeTracker emit time to the first drawn frame showing that angle)
why: delivery latency alone misses the frame Fabric loses waiting for its vsync event beat; users see frames
result: smoke: nitro 7.0 ms vs fabric 25.4 ms p50, one run each

decision: added prototype C, a codegen TurboModule event emitter with no Nitro
why: React Native's AsyncEventEmitter goes through jsInvoker->invokeAsync, the same CallInvoker path as Nitro callbacks, so the speedup may not need Nitro
result: smoke: delivery 0.28 ms, same as nitro

decision: did not build a coalescing Nitro variant
why: under JS load Nitro still drew fresher values than Fabric (12.7 vs 23.3 ms p50) because React batches the queued callbacks

decision: ran the hinge matrix: 4 transports x idle/loaded JS x render on/off, 5 rounds, rotating order, host load 1.6-2.3
why: alternating runs keep warm-up and drift from favouring a transport
result: 50 runs, badT 0 everywhere, clock offset -0.009 ms

decision: hinge to drawn frame: Fabric 23.4 ms p50 vs Nitro 8.2 vs TurboModule 10.2 (idle JS); 25.1 vs 12.3 vs 12.0 under 200 ms JS load
why: the user-visible number; Fabric waits for the next vsync before JS sees the event and then mounts a frame later
evidence: rank-sum p=0.008 Fabric vs Nitro; Nitro vs Turbo p=0.31 idle, 1.0 loaded
result: Fabric slower by about a frame; Nitro = Turbo

decision: dropped the JS commit-split probe without building it
why: the Nitro-vs-Turbo end-to-end gap it was meant to explain did not survive 5 rounds

decision: per-sample CPU: JS 51 us Fabric vs 16.5 Nitro vs 17 Turbo; main thread over the sweep 175 vs 151 vs 168 ms (none 70)
why: Fabric's JS cost is React's event dispatch; Nitro's main-thread saving is skipping the WritableMap
evidence: rank-sum p=0.008 JS Fabric vs Nitro; main Nitro vs Turbo p=0.016
result: real but under 0.3% of either thread at 60 Hz
